9885.explanation:
King Saul asked Jesse to send David to him because he wanted David to serve him. After David had been anointed as the future king by the prophet Samuel, Saul was troubled by an evil spirit, and his servants suggested bringing in a skilled musician to help soothe him. David, who was known for his skill with the lyre, was brought to Saul to play music for him and to serve in the king's court.

1 Samuel 16:21 (RSV):

“And David came to Saul and entered his service. And Saul loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer.”

9905.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
9905.question_text: When the Babylonians captured King Zebekiah they
9905.explanation:
When the Babylonians captured King Zedekiah, the last king of Judah, they took him to Riblah, where they executed a brutal punishment. According to Jeremiah 39:6-7 (RSV):

"Then the king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes; and the king of Babylon slew all the nobles of Judah. He put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him in fetters to take him to Babylon."

Thus, they put out his eyes before taking him to Babylon in chains. This was a symbolic act of total humiliation and loss of hope for Zedekiah, marking the end of the Davidic dynasty's rule.

9919.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
9919.question_text: God decided not to punish the people of Israel during the reign of Josiah for the sins they committed because
9919.explanation:
When King Josiah heard the words of the Book of the Law and realized how Israel had sinned, he tore his clothes in sorrow. Because of his humility and repentance, God delayed His judgment on Israel until after Josiah’s reign.

2 Kings 22:19-20 (RSV) states:
"Because your heart was penitent, and you humbled yourself before the Lord, when you heard how I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants that they should become a desolation and a curse, and you have rent your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, says the Lord. Therefore, behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes shall not see all the evil which I will bring upon this place."

This confirms that Josiah's humility and repentance were the reasons why God postponed the punishment of Israel.

options.text: Josiah humbled himself before the LORD and repented
Josiah walked righteously before the LORD, his God
He did not want Josiah to backslide

9940.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
9940.question_text: Peter teaches that good Christian conduct is characterised by love and
9940.explanation:
In 1 Peter 1:17, Peter teaches that a key characteristic of good Christian conduct is living in reverence or fear of God. This fear is not about being afraid but involves respect, awe and obedience to God. Peter encourages believers to conduct their lives in a way that reflects their relationship with God, especially in how they treat others.

1 Peter 1:17 (RSV):

"If you invoke as Father him who judges impartially according to each one’s deeds, conduct yourselves with fear throughout the time of your exile."

This fear is a deep respect for God's holiness and His judgment.

9946.explanation:
In James 2:1, James addresses believers about not showing partiality. He emphasises that because they hold the faith of the Lord Jesus Christ, they should not show favoritism or discrimination based on outward appearances, social status, or wealth.

James 2:1 (RSV):

"My brothers, show no partiality as you hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory."

James argues that showing partiality goes against the teachings of Christ, who showed no favouritism.

9949.explanation: In phillipians 2 verse 5-11, Paul explains the great humility it took for Jesus Christ to become that little baby in the manger which even this wicked world acknowledges and sings about at Christmas. Paul’s purpose was to exhort the Philippians to be humble by following Christ’s example of humility, but to do so, Paul must first explain the glory Christ had before becoming a man. He then goes on to explain the reason He became a man, what His position is now and what will occur in the future. You cannot understand the humility of Jesus without contrasting it to the glory that actually belongs to Him.
